### SET FREE
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/day-by-day-nov-13-2008-11595665.html
Passage: Job 42:7-9
Points:
- God vindicated Job before his critical friends by repeatedly honoring him as His servant.
- Job's companions had to humble themselves, bring sacrifices, and seek reconciliation.
- Job harbored no bitterness, graciously praying for the men who had judged him harshly.
- Genuine restoration occurs when justice and mercy combine to remove guilt.
- Job's sacrificial intercession foreshadows Christ's atonement on the cross.

### Bible Pathway - June 25, 2012
Author: Bible Pathway
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathway-june-25-2012.html
Passage: Job 42:7
Points:
- Job's companions wrongly assumed earthly prosperity meant God's favor and suffering meant His anger.
- The Lord's rebuke demonstrated that human reasoning fails to discern God's higher purposes.
- God was pleased with Job even when Job could not perceive it through his pain.
- Believers must not evaluate divine providence through carnal or short-sighted perspectives.
- Hardships ultimately serve God's greater, perfect design to yield spiritual fruit.
